hints: Look for the tall peaks in first ionisation energy, they tell you where each period ends.
Notice that B, J and R are the three highest peaks, so each one is followed by a sharp drop to C, K and S.
Count forward from each new low point as Group 1, Group 2, then Group 13 to 18, and see where D, L, G and O land.
walkthrough:
**Spot the noble gases**

Think like a teacher with your student. First ionisation energy jumps up across a period and then crashes down when a new shell starts. The peaks are the hardest to ionise, the full-shell noble gases.

Here B, J and R are the three clear peaks, so they must be Group 18.

**Rebuild the groups after each peak**

After a noble gas, the next element starts a new period with one outer electron. So C, K and S are Group 1 (very low IE), and the next ones D, L and T are Group 2 (a little higher).

Continuing across the p-block:
$$ \text{Group 1} \to \text{Group 2} \to \text{Group 13} \to \text{Group 14} \to \text{Group 15} \to \text{Group 16} \to \text{Group 17} \to \text{Group 18} $$

**Check the two special positions**

Group 2 means outer configuration $ns^2$, so D (after C) and L (after K) both have two outer electrons. Group 15 means $ns^2 np^3$, a half-filled p subshell, which is extra stable and gives a small peak.

On the graph G is the small peak before the dip at H, and O is the small peak before the dip at P. So G and O are both Group 15.

**Conclude on the three statements**

Statement 1 is true, B, J, R are Group 18. Statement 2 is true, D, L are Group 2. Statement 3 is true, G, O are Group 15 with $np^3$.

All three are correct.

options.A: Correct. All three statements are true. B, J, R are noble gas peaks, D and L are the Group 2 elements just after the Group 1 troughs, and G and O are the Group 15 half-filled p elements shown by the small peak then dip pattern.
options.B: Incorrect. This option claims only 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is also correct because G and O show the characteristic Group 15 stability of $ns^2 np^3$, higher than F, N and then dropping to H, P.
options.C: Incorrect. This option leaves out statement 1. B, J and R must be Group 18 because they are the highest first ionisation energies in each cycle, followed by the very low Group 1 values for C, K and S.
options.D: Incorrect. This option claims only statement 1 is correct. Statements 2 and 3 are also correct. A common trap is to miscount the p-block and think D is Group 1, but the first low point C is Group 1, making D Group 2.
